output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initialSupply is multiplied by 10^uint256(decimals) to set the total supply, and mintedAmount is added to balanceOf[target] without a check, allowing the owner to mint an arbitrary large number of tokens.

The transfer function does not check if the balanceOf[_to] + _value is greater than balanceOf[_to], allowing a user to transfer tokens to a smart contract that has no receive function, resulting in a loss of tokens.

The burnFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The _value is subtracted from allowance[_from][msg.sender], but there is no check to ensure that the result is not greater than balanceOf[_from], allowing a user to burn more tokens than the owner has approved.
The mintToken function has a token devalue issue. The owner can mint an arbitrary large amount of tokens, causing the token to become worthless.
The transfer function does not check if the target is a smart contract, allowing attackers to exploit it to create a DOS vulnerability.
